Main.sentence: The Central Intelligence Agency ( CIA /ˌsiː.aɪˈeɪ/ ) is a civilian ___E:foreign intelligence service U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelligence_agency)___ of the ___E:federal government of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_the_United_States)___ tasked with advancing ___E:national security U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_security)___ through collecting and analyzing intelligence from around the world and conducting ___E:covert operations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Covert_operation)___ .

The agency is headquartered in the ___E:George Bush Center for Intelligence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Bush_Center_for_Intelligence)___ in ___E:Langley, Virginia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Langley,_Virginia)___ , and is sometimes ___E:metonymously U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metonymy)___ called "Langley".

A major member of the ___E:United States Intelligence Community U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Intelligence_Community)___ (IC), the CIA has reported to the ___E:director of national intelligence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director_of_National_Intelligence)___ since 2004, and is focused on providing intelligence for the ___E:president U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ and the ___E:Cabinet U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_the_United_States)___ , though it also provides intelligence for a variety of other entities including the ___E:US Military U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Military)___ and foreign allies.

The CIA is headed by ___E:a director U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director_of_the_Central_Intelligence_Agency)___ and is divided into various directorates, including a Directorate of Analysis and ___E:Directorate of Operations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directorate_of_Operations_(CIA))___ .

Unlike the ___E:Federal Bureau of Investigation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation)___ (FBI), the CIA has no law enforcement function and focuses on intelligence gathering overseas, with only ___E:limited domestic intelligence collection U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Resources_Division)___ .

The CIA is responsible for coordinating all ___E:human intelligence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_intelligence_(intelligence_gathering))___ (HUMINT) activities in the IC. It has been instrumental in establishing intelligence services in many countries, and has provided support to many foreign organizations.
The CIA exerts foreign political influence through its paramilitary operations units, including its ___E:Special Activities Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_Activities_Center)___ .

It has also provided support to several foreign political groups and governments, including planning, coordinating, ___E:training and carrying out torture U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enhanced_interrogation_techniques)___ , and technical support.

It was involved in many ___E:regime changes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_involvement_in_regime_change)___ and carrying out planned assassinations of foreign leaders and ___E:terrorist attacks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrorism)___ against civilians.

During ___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)___ , U.S. intelligence and covert operations had been undertaken by the ___E:Office of Strategic Services U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_Strategic_Services)___ (OSS).

The office was abolished in 1945 by President ___E:Harry S. Truman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_S._Truman)___ , who created the ___E:Central Intelligence Group U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Intelligence_Group)___ in 1946. Amid the intensifying ___E:Cold War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War)___ , the ___E:National Security Act of 1947 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Security_Act_of_1947)___ established the CIA, headed by a ___E:director of central intelligence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director_of_Central_Intelligence)___ (DCI).

The ___E:Central Intelligence Agency Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Intelligence_Agency_Act)___ of 1949 exempted the agency from most Congressional oversight, and during the 1950s, it became a major instrument of U.S. foreign policy.

The CIA employed ___E:psychological operations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychological_warfare)___ against communist regimes, and backed ___E:coups to advance American interests U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_involvement_in_regime_change)___ .

Major CIA-backed operations include the ___E:1953 coup in Iran U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1953_Iranian_coup_d%27%C3%A9tat)___ , the ___E:1954 coup in Guatemala U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_Guatemalan_coup_d%27%C3%A9tat)___ , the ___E:Bay of Pigs Invasion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bay_of_Pigs_Invasion)___ of ___E:Cuba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba)___ in 1961, and the ___E:1973 coup in Chile U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1973_Chilean_coup_d%27%C3%A9tat)___ .

In 1975, the ___E:Church Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_Committee)___ of the ___E:U.S. Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate)___ revealed illegal operations such as ___E:MKUltra U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MKUltra)___ and ___E:CHAOS U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_CHAOS)___ , after which greater oversight was imposed.

In the 1980s, the CIA supported the ___E:Afghan mujahideen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghan_mujahideen)___ and Nicaraguan ___E:Contras U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contras)___ , and since the ___E:September 11 attacks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks)___ in 2001 has played a role in the ___E:Global War on Terrorism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_on_terror)___ .

The agency has been the subject of ___E:numerous controversies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_CIA_controversies)___ , including its ___E:use of political assassinations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_rights_violations_by_the_CIA)___ , ___E:torture U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enhanced_interrogation_techniques)___ , ___E:domestic wiretapping U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_Mockingbird)___ , ___E:propaganda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CIA_influence_on_public_opinion)___ , ___E:mind control techniques U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MKUltra)___ , and ___E:drug trafficking U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allegations_of_CIA_drug_trafficking)___ , among others.

When the CIA was created, its purpose was to create a clearinghouse for foreign policy intelligence and analysis, collecting, analyzing, evaluating, and disseminating foreign intelligence, and carrying out covert operations.

The CIA has an executive office and five major directorates:

The ___E:director of the Central Intelligence Agency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director_of_the_Central_Intelligence_Agency)___ (D/CIA) is appointed by the ___E:president U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ with ___E:Senate confirmation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_confirmation)___ and reports directly to the ___E:director of national intelligence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director_of_National_Intelligence)___ (DNI); in practice, the CIA director interfaces with the DNI, ___E:Congress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress)___ , and the ___E:White House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House)___ , while the ___E:deputy director (DD/CIA) U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deputy_Director_of_the_Central_Intelligence_Agency)___ is the internal executive of the CIA and the chief operating officer (COO/CIA), known as executive director until 2017, leads the day-to-day work  as the third-highest post of the CIA.  The deputy director is formally appointed by the director without ___E:Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate)___ confirmation,   but as the president's opinion plays a great role in the decision,  the deputy director is generally considered a political position, making the chief operating officer the most senior non-political position for CIA career officers.

The Executive Office also supports the ___E:U.S. military U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_military)___ , including the ___E:U.S. Army Intelligence and Security Command U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Intelligence_and_Security_Command)___ , by providing it with information it gathers, receiving information from ___E:military intelligence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_intelligence)___ organizations, and cooperating with field activities.
The associate deputy director of the CIA is in charge of the day-to-day operations of the agency.
Each branch of the agency has its own director.

The Office of Military Affairs (OMA), subordinate to the associate deputy director, manages the relationship between the CIA and the ___E:Unified Combatant Commands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unified_Combatant_Command)___ , who produce and deliver regional and operational intelligence and consume national intelligence produced by the CIA.

The Directorate of Analysis , through much of its history known as the Directorate of Intelligence (DI), is tasked with helping "the President and other policymakers make informed decisions about our country's national security" by looking "at all the available information on an issue and organiz[ing] it for policymakers".
The directorate has four regional analytic groups, six groups for transnational issues, and three that focus on policy, collection, and staff support.

There are regional analytical offices covering the ___E:Near East U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Near_East)___ and ___E:South Asia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Asia)___ , ___E:Russia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia)___ , and Europe; and the ___E:Asia–Pacific U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia%E2%80%93Pacific)___ , ___E:Latin America U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_America)___ , and ___E:Africa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Africa)___ .
The Directorate of Operations is responsible for collecting foreign intelligence (mainly from clandestine HUMINT sources), and for covert action.
The name reflects its role as the coordinator of human intelligence activities between other elements of the wider U.S. intelligence community with their HUMINT operations.

This directorate was created in an attempt to end years of rivalry over influence, philosophy, and budget between the ___E:United States Department of Defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Defense)___ (DOD) and the CIA. In spite of this, the Department of Defense announced in 2012 its intention to organize its own global clandestine intelligence service, the ___E:Defense Clandestine Service U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defense_Clandestine_Service)___ (DCS),  under the ___E:Defense Intelligence Agency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defense_Intelligence_Agency)___ (DIA).

Contrary to some public and ___E:media U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mass_media)___ misunderstanding, DCS is not a "new" ___E:intelligence agency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelligence_agency)___ but rather a consolidation, expansion and realignment of existing Defense ___E:HUMINT U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clandestine_HUMINT)___ activities, which have been carried out by DIA for decades under various names, most recently as the Defense Human Intelligence Service.
This Directorate is known to be organized by geographic regions and issues, but its precise organization is classified.
The Directorate of Science & Technology was established to research, create, and manage technical collection disciplines and equipment.
Many of its innovations were transferred to other intelligence organizations, or, as they became more overt, to the military services.

The development of the ___E:U-2 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockheed_U-2)___ high-altitude reconnaissance aircraft, for instance, was done in cooperation with the ___E:United States Air Force U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Air_Force)___ .

The U-2's original mission was clandestine ___E:imagery intelligence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMINT)___ over denied areas such as the ___E:Soviet Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union)___ .

The Directorate of Digital Innovation (DDI) focuses on accelerating innovation across the Agency's mission activities.
It is the Agency's newest directorate.

The ___E:Langley, Virginia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Langley,_Virginia)___ -based office's mission is to streamline and integrate digital and cybersecurity capabilities into the CIA's espionage, counterintelligence, all-source analysis, open-source intelligence collection, and covert action operations.
It provides operations personnel with tools and techniques to use in cyber operations.

It works with ___E:information technology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_technology)___ infrastructure and practices cyber ___E:tradecraft U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tradecraft)___ .
This means retrofitting the CIA for ___E:cyberwarfare U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyberwarfare)___ .
DDI officers help accelerate the integration of innovative methods and tools to enhance the CIA's cyber and digital capabilities on a global scale and ultimately help safeguard the United States.

They also apply technical expertise to exploit clandestine and publicly available information (also known as ___E:open-source data U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-source_intelligence)___ ) using specialized methodologies and digital tools to plan, initiate and support the technical and human-based operations of the CIA.  Before the establishment of the new digital directorate, offensive cyber operations were undertaken by the CIA's Information Operations Center.
Little is known about how the office specifically functions or if it deploys offensive cyber capabilities.

The directorate had been covertly operating since approximately March 2015 but formally began operations on October 1, 2015.  According to classified budget documents, the CIA's computer network operations budget for fiscal year 2013 was $685.4 million.
The NSA's budget was roughly $1 billion at the time.

"The director has challenged his workforce, the rest of the intelligence community, and the nation to consider how we conduct the business of intelligence in a world that is profoundly different from 1947 when the CIA was founded," Schiff said.

The CIA established its first training facility, the Office of Training and Education, in 1950. Following the end of the ___E:Cold War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War)___ , the CIA's training budget was slashed, which had a negative effect on ___E:employee retention U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Employee_retention)___ .

In response, Director of Central Intelligence ___E:George Tenet U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Tenet)___ established ___E:CIA University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CIA_University)___ in 2002.   CIA University holds between 200 and 300 courses each year, training both new hires and experienced intelligence officers, as well as CIA support staff.

The facility works in partnership with the ___E:National Intelligence University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Intelligence_University)___ , and includes the ___E:Sherman Kent School for Intelligence Analysis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherman_Kent_School_for_Intelligence_Analysis)___ , the Directorate of Analysis' component of the university.

For later stage training of student operations officers, there is at least one classified training area at ___E:Camp Peary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Peary)___ , near ___E:Williamsburg, Virginia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williamsburg,_Virginia)___ .
Students are selected, and their progress evaluated, in ways derived from the OSS, published as the book Assessment of Men, Selection of Personnel for the Office of Strategic Services .
Additional mission training is conducted at ___E:Harvey Point U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvey_Point)___ , ___E:North Carolina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina)___ .

The primary training facility for the Office of Communications is ___E:Warrenton Training Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warrenton_Training_Center)___ , located near ___E:Warrenton, Virginia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warrenton,_Virginia)___ .
The facility was established in 1951 and has been used by the CIA since at least 1955.
Details of the overall United States intelligence budget are classified.

Under the ___E:Central Intelligence Agency Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Intelligence_Agency_Act)___ of 1949, the Director of Central Intelligence is the only federal government employee who can spend ___E:"un-vouchered" government money U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_budget)___ .

The government showed its 1997 budget was $26.6 billion for the fiscal year.  The government has disclosed a total figure for all non-military intelligence spending since 2007; the fiscal 2013 figure is $52.6 billion.

According to the ___E:2013 mass surveillance disclosures U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_mass_surveillance_disclosures)___ , the CIA's fiscal 2013 budget is $14.7 billion, 28% of the total and almost 50% more than the budget of the National Security Agency.

CIA's ___E:HUMINT U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HUMINT)___ budget is $2.3 billion, the ___E:SIGINT U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIGINT)___ budget is $1.7 billion, and spending for security and logistics of CIA missions is $2.5 billion. "Covert action programs," including a variety of activities such as the CIA's ___E:drone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unmanned_combat_aerial_vehicle)___ fleet and anti- ___E:Iranian nuclear program U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iranian_nuclear_program)___ activities, accounts for $2.6 billion.
There were numerous previous attempts to obtain general information about the budget.

As a result, reports revealed that CIA's annual budget in Fiscal Year 1963 was $550 million (equivalent to US$5.6 billion in 2024),  and the overall intelligence budget in FY 1997 was US$26.6 billion (equivalent to US$52.1 billion in 2024).

There have been accidental disclosures; for instance, ___E:Mary Margaret Graham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Margaret_Graham)___ , a former CIA official and deputy director of national intelligence for collection in 2005, said that the annual intelligence budget was $44 billion,  and in 1994 Congress accidentally published a budget of $43.4 billion (in 2012 dollars) in 1994 for the non-military National Intelligence Program, including $4.8 billion for the CIA.

After the ___E:Marshall Plan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshall_Plan)___ was approved, appropriating $13.7 billion over five years, 5% of those funds or $685 million were secretly made available to the CIA. A portion of the enormous M-fund, established by the U.S. government during the post-war period for reconstruction of Japan, was secretly steered to the CIA.

The CIA was instrumental in the establishment of intelligence services in several U.S. allied countries, including Germany's BND and Greece's ___E:EYP U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Intelligence_Service_(Greece))___ (then known as KYP).  [citation needed]
The closest links of the U.S. intelligence community to other foreign intelligence agencies are to Anglophone countries: Australia, Canada, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom.
Special communications signals that intelligence-related messages can be shared with these four countries.
An indication of the United States' close operational cooperation is the creation of a new message distribution label within the main U.S. military communications network.
Previously, the marking of NOFORN (i.e., No Foreign Nationals) required the originator to specify which, if any, non-U.S. countries could receive the information.
A new handling caveat, USA/AUS/CAN/GBR/NZL Five Eyes , used primarily on intelligence messages, indicates that the material can be shared with Australia, Canada, United Kingdom, and New Zealand.
The task of the division called " Verbindungsstelle 61 " of the German Bundesnachrichtendienst is keeping contact to the CIA office in ___E:Wiesbaden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiesbaden)___ .

During ___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)___ , U.S. intelligence and covert operations were undertaken by the ___E:Office of Strategic Services U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_Strategic_Services)___ (OSS).

Many future CIA officers, including four directors of Central Intelligence, served in the OSS.  On September 20, 1945, shortly after the end of World War II, Truman signed an ___E:executive order U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_order_(United_States))___ dissolving the OSS.  By October 1945 its functions had been divided between the ___E:Departments of State U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_State)___ and ___E:War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_War)___ .
The division lasted only a few months.

The first public mention of the "Central Intelligence Agency" appeared on a command-restructuring proposal presented by ___E:Jim Forrestal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Forrestal)___ and ___E:Arthur Radford U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Radford)___ to the ___E:U.S. Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Senate)___ Military Affairs Committee at the end of 1945.  Army Intelligence agent Colonel ___E:Sidney Mashbir U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sidney_Mashbir)___ and Commander Ellis Zacharias worked together for four months at the direction of ___E:Fleet Admiral Joseph Ernest King U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernest_King)___ , and prepared the first draft and implementing directives for the creation of what would become the Central Intelligence Agency.

Despite opposition from the military establishment, the ___E:State Department U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_State)___ , and the ___E:Federal Bureau of Investigation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation)___ (FBI),  Truman established the ___E:National Intelligence Authority U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Intelligence_Authority_(United_States))___  in January 1946. Its operational extension was known as the Central Intelligence Group (CIG),  which was the direct predecessor of the CIA.

The Central Intelligence Agency was created on July 26, 1947, when President Truman signed the ___E:National Security Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Security_Act_of_1947)___ into law. A major impetus for the creation of the agency was growing tensions with the USSR following the end of ___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)___ .

Lawrence Houston, head counsel of the ___E:SSU U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strategic_Services_Unit)___ , CIG, and, later CIA, was principal draftsman of the ___E:National Security Act of 1947 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Security_Act_of_1947)___ ,    which dissolved the NIA and the CIG, and established both the ___E:National Security Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_National_Security_Council)___ and the Central Intelligence Agency.

In 1949, Houston helped to draft the ___E:Central Intelligence Agency Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Intelligence_Agency_Act)___ ( ___E:Pub. L. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Act_of_Congress#Public_law,_private_law,_designation)___ ___E:81–110 U:(https://uslaw.link/citation/us-law/public/81/110)___ ), which authorized the agency to use confidential fiscal and administrative procedures, and exempted it from most limitations on the use of federal funds.

The act also exempted the CIA from having to disclose its "organization, functions, officials, titles, salaries, or numbers of personnel employed," and created the program "PL-110" to handle defectors and other "essential aliens" who fell outside normal immigration procedures.
At the outset of the ___E:Korean War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_War)___ , the CIA still only had a few thousand employees, around one thousand of whom worked in analysis.
Intelligence primarily came from the Office of Reports and Estimates, which drew its reports from a daily take of State Department telegrams, military dispatches, and other public documents.
The CIA still lacked its intelligence-gathering abilities.

On August 21, 1950, shortly after, Truman announced ___E:Walter Bedell Smith U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Bedell_Smith)___ as the new Director of the CIA. The change in leadership took place shortly after the start of the ___E:Korean War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_War)___ in ___E:South Korea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korea)___ , as the lack of a clear warning to the President and NSC about the imminent North Korean invasion was seen as a grave failure of intelligence.

The CIA had different demands placed on it by the various bodies overseeing it. Truman wanted a centralized group to organize the information that reached him.   The Department of Defense wanted military intelligence and covert action, and the State Department wanted to create global political change favorable to the US. Thus the two areas of responsibility for the CIA were covert action and covert intelligence.

One of the main targets for intelligence gathering was the ___E:Soviet Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_of_Soviet_Socialist_Republics)___ , which had also been a priority of the CIA's predecessors.
U.S.

Air Force General ___E:Hoyt Vandenberg U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoyt_Vandenberg)___ , the CIG's second director, created the Office of Special Operations (OSO) and the Office of Reports and Estimates (ORE).
Initially, the OSO was tasked with spying and subversion overseas with a budget of $15 million (equivalent to $196 million in 2024),  the largesse of a small number of patrons in Congress.

Vandenberg's goals were much like the ones set out by his predecessor: finding out "everything about the Soviet forces in Eastern and Central Europe – their movements, their capabilities, and their intentions."

On June 18, 1948, the ___E:National Security Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Security_Council)___ issued Directive 10/2  calling for covert action against the ___E:Soviet Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union)___ ,  and granting the authority to carry out covert operations against "hostile foreign states or groups" that could, if needed, be denied by the U.S. government.

To this end, the ___E:Office of Policy Coordination U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_Policy_Coordination)___ (OPC) was created inside the CIA.
